claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a metastable BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder has a high defect density and may contain oxygen contamination.
SPS at 950–1000 °C under 30 MPa for 15 minutes is an appropriate processing window.
Vacuum or inert argon minimizes oxidation during milling and sintering.
Temperatures above 800 °C provide sufficient atomic mobility, whereas temperatures above 1000 °C cause problematic Mg volatility.
Sintering at 950–1000 °C produces a percolating nanoscale network of (Al,Ti)-rich BCC intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Rapid diffusion of Al and Ti drives precipitation of the grain-boundary intermetallic network.
At 950–1000 °C, the driving force for phase separation overcomes configurational entropy and causes Al and Ti segregation and intermetallic formation.
The (Al,Ti)-rich precipitate network acts as a diffusion barrier that suppresses Mg evaporation.
The precipitates pin grain boundaries, slow grain growth, and thereby densify the bulk.
The precipitate network facilitates formation of a dense Cr/Al/Ti-oxide passive layer during subsequent exposure.
The alloy sintered in the proposed window will reach greater than 95% theoretical density.
The alloy sintered in the proposed window will exceed 400 HV Vickers hardness.
The alloy sintered in the proposed window will have a corrosion current density at least one order of magnitude below that of material sintered at 750 °C.
Samples sintered at 750 °C will remain porous, retain a homogeneous BCC solid solution, and exhibit poor corrosion resistance.
Samples sintered at 1050 °C will undergo Mg depletion, become porous, and lose the protective barrier mechanism.
Mg loss above 1000 °C changes local stoichiometry and prevents formation of the proposed (Al,Ti)-rich barrier phase.
Exceeding the temperature boundary leads to brittle, non-protective oxides or porosity.
Parabolic oxidation kinetics indicate diffusion control, whereas linear kinetics indicate surface-reaction control.
Absence of a continuous (Al,Ti)-rich network or observation of linear oxidation kinetics in the 975 °C batch would falsify the proposed diffusion-barrier mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention and hypothesis include sintering at exactly 1000 °C, while the conditions require the temperature to be strictly below 1000 °C.
The stated alloy contains Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co but no Cr, yet the mechanism predicts formation of a Cr-containing passive oxide layer without identifying any Cr source.
